what: 0.2.3: several conversations decoding at once - the MoE router and the routed experts of a 5-32-token batch on the vector kernel (apply_small_batch_decode), drafts of 2 for up to four conversations (the manager's cap 3,2,2,2,0), TheRock ROCm 10.2.0a20260925
setup: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, the manager's profile with parallel=4 (8 for six and eight conversations), ctx 262144, f16 K/V, MTP with draft_max 3. tmp/kvr/bs_sweep.py on a server started as production (tmp/kvr/with_server.py): N conversations of distinct real text (tmp/realtext.txt slices of 14500 characters, ~4K tokens) pinned to slots and cached first, then N x 512 tokens at once (128 or 256 where stated); tok/s summed over the conversations, wall clock.
question: the user: several conversations at once is what matters most - three conversations should get about twice one conversation's tokens, and the measure is how much of the memory bandwidth a step uses

release_ab.method: 0.2.2 as released (tmp/rt022: ROCm 10.1.0a20260910, cap 3,2,2,0, so four conversations do not draft) against the 0.2.3 build (ROCm 10.2.0a20260925, cap 3,2,2,2,0), alternating, three passes of two rounds, 512 tokens a stream, the server's default sampling (tmp/kvr/rel023_ab.sh)
release_ab.reading: three conversations +17% (1.26x one conversation -> 1.47x), four +9% (1.46x -> 1.59x). One conversation is unchanged: its verify step is at most 4 tokens, which neither change touches, and its acceptance is the same 63% in every run (the 36.0 / 36.4 pass is run-to-run spread). 0.2.3 spreads more at 3 and 4: its acceptance moves between ~65% and ~72% from round to round where 0.2.2's stays at 66-67%, so the sampled text differs between rounds (not traced to a cause).

router.what: the MoE router, an F32 [2560 x 512] product, is past the vector kernel (mul_mat_vec_f, up to 8 columns) at 9 columns and went to MMB's F32 kernel, whose 128 x 128 tiles give four workgroups for the whole GPU: ~250 us a product. STRIX_F32_VEC_CHUNK_MAX=32: an F32 weight at 9-32 columns runs the vector kernel over column chunks, as weights of up to 64 rows already did

ab_3_streams_drafts_of_2.method: tmp/kvr/ms_router.sh: 3 conversations, drafts of 2 (a 9-token verify), 128 tokens a stream, two runs of three rounds; verify_ms is the target's verify step with STRIX_SPEC_TIMING=1 (timing syncs included)

routed_experts.what: past the vector kernel's limit (IQ3_S 4 tokens, IQ4_NL 6 on RDNA 3.5) the routed experts took the tiled MMQ kernel, which stages a tile per expert for the one or two tokens an expert gets; STRIX_MOE_VEC_CHUNK=4 runs chunks of 4 tokens through the vector kernel up to STRIX_MOE_VEC_CHUNK_MAX_T=16 tokens

per_product_us.method: tmp/kvr/moe_bench.sh: one routed-expert product, 512 experts, 10 a token, random routing; gate/up IQ3_S 2560 -> 640, down IQ4_NL 640 -> 2560
per_product_us.note: 4 tokens and IQ4_NL at 6 already ran the vector kernel; the differences there are noise

routed_experts.step: -5 ms of a nine-token verify (verify_ms above: 109 -> 104)

draft_cap.method: STRIX_SPEC_DRAFT_BY_SLOTS with both chunk changes on, 512 tokens a stream (256 at six and eight, greedy), tmp/kvr/ms_capsweep.sh and ms_wide.sh; medians of two rounds

deep_20k.method: tmp/kvr/ms_deep_023.sh: four conversations at ~20K tokens each (slices of 75000 characters), the 0.2.3 build, 512 tokens a stream, the server's default sampling, two runs of two rounds, alternating

draft_cap.reading: with the chunks, drafts of 2 pay at four conversations (+12% at ~4K tokens each, +11% at ~20K) and lose from six on, so the manager's cap is 3,2,2,2,0: three drafts for one conversation, two for two to four, none from five on (five unmeasured, between the two)

rocm_10_2.method: the same source (router and expert chunks on, cap 3,2,2,2) built against TheRock 10.1.0a20260910 and 10.2.0a20260925, alternating, two runs each (tmp/kvr/sdk_ab.sh): prefill of 95.6K tokens of real text, then 512 tokens a stream, greedy
rocm_10_2.checks: perplexity at 8K context, 8 chunks: 2.6814 on both; the 18.6K-token equivalence probe gives the same text and top-5 probabilities bit for bit; truncation --fill passes
rocm_10_2.reading: prefill and one conversation the same (10.2's 37.2 is one round of 33.5, a stall); three and four conversations +3-4%. The pin moves to 10.2.0a20260925: 10.1.0a20260910, the last 10.1 nightly, leaves the index's ~27-day window in early October.

utilization.method: Task Manager's GPU engine counter while decoding (tmp/kvr/ms_util.sh), 12 samples of 1 s, both chunk changes on
utilization.reading: at three conversations the GPU is busy ~89% of the time; what is left is mostly in the step itself: a verify step costs ~55 / 78 / 103 / 127 ms at 3 / 6 / 9 / 12 tokens, ~8 ms a further token of which ~5 is routed-expert weights read near the memory's bandwidth, the rest per-sequence GDN, attention and small kernels

ruled_out.backend_sampling: --backend-sampling at 3 streams, drafts of 2: 55.0 / 53.5 against 55.6 / 55.8 with CPU sampling (tmp/kvr/ms_bsamp.sh)
ruled_out.dense_q8_0_small_batches: the dense Q8_0 products read ~216 GB/s up to 8 columns and are 8-10% slower at 9-16 on MMQ; a node-timing profile with graphs off had made it look larger

checks.gates: tmp/kvr/gates_023.sh on the built runtime: the 18.6K equivalence probe (f16, MTP off) is bitwise 0.2.2; truncation --fill 79000 and the four-slot agent workload pass; perplexity 2.6814
